Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a **base case** — a condition that stops the recursion — otherwise it would call itself forever. Each call adds to the **call stack**, and when the base case is finally reached, the results "unwind" back up, with each call returning its answer to the one below it. Think of it like nesting Russian dolls: you keep opening smaller dolls until you reach the smallest one, then put them all back together on your way out.
